title: Inline Editing: A UX System
summary: This lesson breaks down the technical and design requirements for seamless inline editing, focusing on affordances, layout stability, and state management. It emphasizes that inline editing is not just a UI swap but a system of behaviors including keyboard semantics and optimistic updates.

transcript.text: Click the title. It's an input now. Nothing moved.
Editable text has to whisper it. A pencil on hover, a soft background tint.
No signal, and users file tickets to change a title.
The swap keeps every pixel in place. Same font, same size, same padding. Border made transparent.
One jump, and the illusion collapses.
Enter commits. Escape cancels. Everyone agrees.
Blur is the fight. Notion saves on click-away. Spreadsheets discard. Pick one rule and never break it.
Save optimistically. The text updates on screen while the request is still flying.
If the server fails, roll back. Keep the draft. Say why.
Airtable makes every cell editable. Docs make you ask.
More power means more accidents. Match the mode to the cost of a typo.
Inline editing is a system. Follow for more UX engineering. Save this for your next editor.

on_screen_text: AFFORDANCE: Editable has to whisper it
A pencil costs nothing. Tickets don't.
ZERO LAYOUT SHIFT: Same box, different chrome
One jump, and the illusion collapses.
KEYBOARD SEMANTICS: Enter commits. Blur is the fight.
Pick one blur rule. Never break it.
OPTIMISTIC SAVE: Update first. Ask later.
Roll back. Keep the draft. Say why.
EDIT MODES: Match the mode to the cost of a typo
design_principles: Blur Behavior Consistency (Save vs Discard on blur)
Graceful Error Handling (Rollback with draft preservation)
Contextual Edit Modes (Direct vs Explicit based on risk)
before_after: The 'Bad Swap' shows a +3px layout shift when transitioning from text to input, while 'The Swap' maintains 0px shift by matching font, size, and padding exactly.
